title: You Do Not Need 20 Percent Down To Buy A Home

beats.say: You do not need twenty percent down to buy a home, and most first time buyers do not put that much down.
beats.visual: a quiet front door of a small house at golden hour, no people

beats.say: Twenty percent is one of the most repeated numbers in money.
beats.visual: a stack of twenty identical gold coins beside one coin set apart, black marble

beats.say: But in a national survey of buyers, first time buyers put down a median of about ten percent.
beats.visual: an open wallet with a small handful of coins on a wooden table, soft window light

beats.say: Across all buyers, the median was about nineteen percent.
beats.visual: a for sale sign leaning against an empty porch in morning light, no text

beats.say: There are also loans built for smaller down payments.
beats.visual: three different brass keys fanned out on a dark table, hard rim light

beats.say: An FHA loan can require as little as three and a half percent, if your credit score is high enough.
beats.visual: a short wooden step stool beside a tall shelf, warm light, no people

beats.say: Some conventional loans go as low as three percent.
beats.visual: a small stack of coins beside a miniature wooden house model, macro, soft light

beats.say: Here is the part nobody tells you. Twenty percent is not a rule. It is where one extra fee usually stops.
beats.callout: 20% IS A LINE, NOT A RULE
beats.visual: a painted white line crossing an empty road at dawn, no people

beats.say: Below twenty percent, lenders often add mortgage insurance, which protects the lender, not you.
beats.visual: a heavy umbrella held over a small house in the rain, no people

beats.say: The honest catch: a smaller down payment means a bigger loan, a monthly insurance cost, and more interest over time.
beats.visual: a stormy sea with waves rising and falling under a heavy sky and a lighthouse

beats.say: Closing costs also come on top. Run the full numbers, not just the down payment.
beats.visual: a hand holding a magnifying glass over an old printed page, close-up, no face

beats.say: So the myth is that you must wait for twenty percent. The truth is, it is a trade with a price.
beats.visual: an old paper map being unfolded on a wooden table, hands out of focus

beats.say: Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: an empty highway stretching toward a glowing sunrise horizon, wide shot

caption: You do not need 20% down: first-time buyers put down a median of about 10% (NAR 2025), and FHA loans can be 3.5%. The catch: bigger loan, mortgage insurance. Educational content, not financial advice.
description: Many people believe you need 20 percent down to buy a home. The median first-time buyer put down about 10 percent, and some loans ask for as little as 3.5 percent. The myth, the rule and the honest catch.
first_comment: What did you think you needed to put down? Educational only, not financial advice.

facts.claim: NAR 2025 Profile: median down payment 10% for first-time buyers, 19% for all buyers
facts.basis: NAR 2025 Profile of Home Buyers and Sellers

facts.claim: FHA loans allow 3.5% down with a credit score of 580 or higher
Conventional loans can go as low as 3% down; under 20% usually adds private mortgage insurance (PMI)
facts.basis: Fannie Mae; CFPB 'What is private mortgage insurance?'

facts.claim: Catch: smaller down payment means a bigger loan, PMI and more interest
